warm.s: I worked as a receptionist in a hotel from 2019 to 2021, and since then I've been working as a marketing assistant for a travel company.
q: Hiện nay người nói đang làm công việc gì?
What is the speaker's job now?
e: “since then I've been working as a marketing assistant” – hiện tại hoàn thành tiếp diễn = vẫn đang làm. Công việc lễ tân dùng quá khứ đơn “worked … from 2019 to 2021” nên đã kết thúc.
“since then I've been working as a marketing assistant” – present perfect continuous = still doing it. The receptionist job uses the past simple “worked … from 2019 to 2021”, so it has ended.

warm.s: I have three years of experience in marketing.
e: “experience” là danh từ không đếm được ở nghĩa kinh nghiệm: không thêm -s. Giới từ: experience in + lĩnh vực.
“experience” (= knowledge from work) is uncountable: no -s. Preposition: experience in + field.

warm.s: My main strength is teamwork.
e: “strength” có cụm phụ âm khó /streŋθ/ – viết đủ “ng” và “th”. “teamwork” viết liền.
“strength” has a hard consonant cluster /streŋθ/ – write both “ng” and “th”. “teamwork” is one word.

warm.s: I've been working at ABC since 2022.
e: I've = I have; been working = tiếp diễn. Since + mốc thời gian (2022); for + khoảng thời gian.
I've = I have; been working = continuous. Since + a point in time (2022); for + a period.

warm.s: In five years, I hope I will have become a team leader, and I would like to manage my own projects and help new colleagues learn the job.
e: Câu hỏi: Where do you see yourself in five years? – Gợi ý trả lời mẫu. Đọc rõ “will have become”.
Question: Where do you see yourself in five years? – Model answer. Say “will have become” clearly.

warm.s: You should hire me because I have three years of experience in sales, I learn quickly, and I have always been good at building relationships with clients.
e: Câu hỏi: Why should we hire you? – Gợi ý trả lời mẫu. Nhấn vào “experience”, “quickly”, “relationships”.
Question: Why should we hire you? – Model answer. Stress “experience”, “quickly” and “relationships”.

hard.s: Nếu được nhận, tôi muốn biết khi nào tôi có thể bắt đầu và liệu có thời gian thử việc không.
a: If I were offered the job, I'd like to know when I could start and whether there would be a probation period.
If I'm offered the position, I'd like to know when I can start and whether there's a probation period.
If I were offered the job, I would like to know when I could start and if there would be a probationary period.
If I get the job, I'd like to know when I could start and whether there's a probation period.
e: Câu hỏi gián tiếp: “I'd like to know when I could start” (không đảo ngữ “when could I start”); “whether” = liệu. “probation period” = thời gian thử việc.
Indirect questions keep normal word order: “when I could start”, not “when could I start”; “whether” = if. “probation period” = trial period.
f: whether there would be a probation period

q: Tường thuật lại câu hỏi của người phỏng vấn, bắt đầu bằng “She asked me …”.
Report the interviewer's question, starting with “She asked me …”.
hard.s: “Why did you leave your last job?”
a: She asked me why I had left my last job.
She asked me why I'd left my last job.
She asked me why I left my last job.
e: Câu hỏi tường thuật: bỏ “did”, giữ trật tự chủ ngữ + động từ, lùi thì: left → had left. Không viết “why did I leave”.
Reported questions drop “did”, use subject + verb order and backshift: left → had left. Not “why did I leave”.
f: why I had left my last job

hard.s: To be honest, I'd rather not to talk about my current salary, but I'm happy to tell you what I'm looking for in this role.
a: To be honest, I'd rather not talk about my current salary, but I'm happy to tell you what I'm looking for in this role.
e: “would rather (not) + động từ nguyên mẫu không to”: I'd rather not talk. Đây là cách khéo léo để né câu hỏi về lương hiện tại.
“would rather (not) + bare infinitive”: I'd rather not talk. It is a tactful way to avoid a question about your current pay.

hard.s: I'm hoping to get my foot in the ___ at a big agency, even if it means starting as an intern for a few months.
a: door
e: “get your foot in the door” = có được bước chân đầu tiên vào công ty/ngành – thành ngữ phổ biến khi nói về xin việc.
“get your foot in the door” = get a first chance to enter a company or industry – a common job-hunting idiom.
f: get my foot in the door

rd2.tx: Last spring I applied for a position as a marketing assistant at a travel company in Da Nang. I had sent more than twenty CVs, so I was nervous when they finally invited me to an interview. The manager started with a simple question: “Why do you want to work here?” I explained that I had been following the company's social media for a year and that I really admired its campaigns. Then she asked about my strengths and weaknesses. I said my main strength is teamwork, but I sometimes spend too long on small details. To show my experience, I used the STAR method: I described a situation at my old job, the task I was given, the action I took and the result. When she asked about my expected salary, I gave a realistic range instead of a single number. Two days after the interview, I sent a short thank-you email. A week later, they offered me the job, and I've been working there since June.
rd2.tr: Mùa xuân năm ngoái tôi ứng tuyển vị trí trợ lý marketing ở một công ty du lịch tại Đà Nẵng. Tôi đã gửi hơn hai mươi bộ CV, nên tôi rất hồi hộp khi cuối cùng họ mời tôi đi phỏng vấn. Chị quản lý bắt đầu bằng một câu hỏi đơn giản: “Tại sao bạn muốn làm việc ở đây?” Tôi giải thích rằng tôi đã theo dõi mạng xã hội của công ty suốt một năm và rất ngưỡng mộ các chiến dịch của họ. Sau đó chị hỏi về điểm mạnh và điểm yếu của tôi. Tôi nói điểm mạnh chính của tôi là làm việc nhóm, nhưng đôi khi tôi mất quá nhiều thời gian vào chi tiết nhỏ. Để thể hiện kinh nghiệm, tôi dùng phương pháp STAR: tôi mô tả một tình huống ở công việc cũ, nhiệm vụ được giao, hành động tôi đã làm và kết quả. Khi chị hỏi về mức lương mong muốn, tôi đưa ra một khoảng hợp lý thay vì một con số duy nhất. Hai ngày sau buổi phỏng vấn, tôi gửi một email cảm ơn ngắn. Một tuần sau, họ nhận tôi vào làm, và tôi làm ở đó từ tháng Sáu.

q: Vì sao người viết hồi hộp khi được mời phỏng vấn?
Why was the writer nervous about the interview?
o: Vì đã gửi hơn 20 CV mà mới được mời
Because they had sent over 20 CVs before getting an invitation
Because they had never worked before
Because they didn't like the company
e: “I had sent more than twenty CVs, so I was nervous” – lý do nằm ở số CV đã gửi. Người viết có “old job” nên đã từng đi làm.
“I had sent more than twenty CVs, so I was nervous” – the reason is the number of CVs. The writer mentions an “old job”, so they had worked before.
f: I had sent more than twenty CVs

q: Người viết trả lời câu hỏi về lương như thế nào?
How did the writer answer the salary question?
o: Đưa ra một khoảng hợp lý
Nói một con số chính xác
e: “I gave a realistic range instead of a single number” – instead of = thay vì, nên đáp án “một con số” là sai.
“I gave a realistic range instead of a single number” – instead of means “not”, so “one exact number” is wrong.
f: a realistic range instead of a single number

q: Câu nào đúng về công việc hiện tại của người viết?
Which is true about the writer's job now?
o: Họ vẫn đang làm ở công ty đó từ tháng Sáu
They have worked there since June and still do
Họ đã nghỉ việc vào tháng Sáu
They left the job in June
Họ vẫn đang chờ kết quả
They are still waiting for the result
e: “I've been working there since June” – hiện tại hoàn thành tiếp diễn: bắt đầu từ tháng Sáu và vẫn tiếp tục.
“I've been working there since June” – present perfect continuous: it began in June and continues now.
f: I've been working there since June

ex2.s: I've been ___ here since 2022, and in that time I have managed three big projects for the company. (work)
a: working
e: have been + V-ing: hiện tại hoàn thành tiếp diễn cho việc vẫn đang làm. Không viết “been work” hay “been worked”.
have been + -ing: present perfect continuous for a job you still do. Not “been work” or “been worked”.

ex2.s: I ___ at ABC from 2019 to 2021, and then I moved to Ho Chi Minh City to study for a master's degree. (work)
a: worked
e: “from 2019 to 2021” là khoảng thời gian đã kết thúc → quá khứ đơn worked, không dùng have worked.
“from 2019 to 2021” is a finished period → past simple worked, not have worked.

ex2.s: I'm good ___ solving problems, so my last manager often asked me to deal with difficult customers on the phone.
a: at
e: be good at + V-ing/danh từ. Lỗi hay gặp: “good in” hoặc “good for”.
be good at + -ing/noun. Common mistakes: “good in” or “good for”.

ex2.s: Before I joined my current company, I ___ as a freelance designer for almost two years, which taught me how to manage my own time.
e: “Before I joined my current company” = việc đã kết thúc trước hiện tại → quá khứ đơn worked. “have been working” chỉ việc còn tiếp diễn.
“Before I joined my current company” = finished before now → past simple worked. “have been working” means it still continues.

ex2.s: I work in the customer service department since 2021, so I know how to handle complaints calmly and quickly.
a: I've been working in the customer service department since 2021, so I know how to handle complaints calmly and quickly.
I have been working in the customer service department since 2021, so I know how to handle complaints calmly and quickly.
I've worked in the customer service department since 2021, so I know how to handle complaints calmly and quickly.
I have worked in the customer service department since 2021, so I know how to handle complaints calmly and quickly.
e: “since 2021” + việc vẫn tiếp tục → hiện tại hoàn thành (tiếp diễn), không dùng hiện tại đơn “I work”.
“since 2021” + an ongoing situation → present perfect (continuous), not the present simple “I work”.

ex2.s: During my last job I was responsible for a team of five people, and I have improved our sales by twenty percent in one year.
a: During my last job I was responsible for a team of five people, and I improved our sales by twenty percent in one year.
e: “During my last job” là công việc đã kết thúc → quá khứ đơn improved. Trong CV, thành tích ở công việc cũ luôn dùng quá khứ đơn.
“During my last job” is a finished job → past simple improved. On a CV, achievements in past jobs always use the past simple.

q: Viết lại câu dùng hiện tại hoàn thành tiếp diễn với “for”.
Rewrite the sentence using the present perfect continuous with “for”.
ex2.s: I started working as a sales assistant three years ago, and I still work in the same department today.
a: I've been working as a sales assistant for three years.
I have been working as a sales assistant for three years.
I've been working as a sales assistant in the same department for three years.
I have been working as a sales assistant in the same department for three years.
e: started … three years ago + still → have been working … for three years. “for” đi với khoảng thời gian, không dùng “since three years”.
started … three years ago + still → have been working … for three years. Use “for” with a period, never “since three years”.
f: have been working as a sales assistant for three years

ex2.s: Tôi có thể bắt đầu làm từ tháng sau.
a: I can start next month.
I could start next month.
I can start work next month.
I'm able to start next month.
e: “next month” không cần giới từ (không viết “from next month” trong câu ngắn này, dù vẫn hiểu được).
“next month” needs no preposition here; “start from next month” sounds less natural.

ex2.s: Công ty có cơ hội đào tạo không?
a: Are there any training opportunities?
Does the company offer any training opportunities?
Are there any training opportunities at the company?
Does the company have any training opportunities?
e: “Are there any … ?” để hỏi có hay không; “training opportunities” = cơ hội đào tạo.
Use “Are there any … ?” to ask if something exists; “training opportunities” = chances to be trained.

ex2.s: Khi còn là sinh viên, tôi làm thêm ở một quán cà phê, nơi tôi học được cách làm việc nhóm dưới áp lực.
a: When I was a student, I worked part-time in a café, where I learned how to work in a team under pressure.
When I was a student, I had a part-time job in a café, where I learned how to work in a team under pressure.
When I was a student, I worked part-time at a coffee shop, where I learned to work in a team under pressure.
As a student, I worked part-time in a café, where I learned how to work as part of a team under pressure.
e: Việc đã kết thúc → quá khứ đơn worked/learned. “where” nối mệnh đề quan hệ chỉ nơi chốn; “under pressure” = dưới áp lực.
A finished period → past simple worked/learned. “where” introduces a relative clause of place; “under pressure” = with stress.

ex2.s: In my previous job|I was asked|to reduce delivery times,|so I introduced|a new tracking system|and cut delays|by almost half
m: Ở công việc trước, tôi được giao giảm thời gian giao hàng, nên tôi đưa vào một hệ thống theo dõi mới và giảm gần một nửa thời gian trễ.
In my previous job I was asked to reduce delivery times, so I introduced a new tracking system and cut delays by almost half.
e: Câu trả lời STAR rút gọn: tình huống/nhiệm vụ (was asked to …) → hành động (introduced …) → kết quả (cut delays by …).
A short STAR answer: situation/task (was asked to …) → action (introduced …) → result (cut delays by …).

q: Viết thư cảm ơn sau phỏng vấn khoảng 100 từ: cảm ơn, nhắc lại 1 điểm mạnh, khẳng định mong muốn làm việc.
Write a thank-you email after an interview (about 100 words): thank the interviewer, mention one strength again, confirm that you want the job.
ex2.m:
Subject: Thank you – Marketing Assistant interview

Dear Ms Hoa,

Thank you for taking the time to meet me yesterday to discuss the Marketing Assistant position. I really enjoyed learning more about your summer campaign and the team's plans for next year.

As I mentioned, I have been managing social media accounts for a local café for two years, and I increased its followers by forty percent. I am confident that this experience would help your team reach more young travellers.

I am very interested in joining your company and would be happy to provide any further information.

I look forward to hearing from you.

Kind regards,
Nguyen Thu Trang
e: Cần có: lời cảm ơn + vị trí đã phỏng vấn; 1 điểm mạnh kèm bằng chứng (con số); khẳng định mong muốn; câu kết lịch sự (I look forward to hearing from you).
Include: thanks + the position; one strength with evidence (a number); a clear wish to join; a polite closing (I look forward to hearing from you).

t: Khách sạn & dịch vụ khách hàng
th:
**Ngữ pháp 1 – động từ khuyết thiếu lịch sự**
• Xin phép: **May I** take your name, please? / May I see your passport?
• Mời, đề nghị: **Would you like** a room with a sea view? / Would you like me to call a taxi?
• Hỏi giúp: **How may I help you?** (trang trọng hơn How can I help you?)
• Khách nói: **Could I** have a late check-out? / I was wondering if I could …

**Grammar 1 – polite modals**
• Asking permission: **May I** take your name, please? / May I see your passport?
• Offering: **Would you like** a room with a sea view? / Would you like me to call a taxi?
• Offering help: **How may I help you?** (more formal than How can I help you?)
• Guests say: **Could I** have a late check-out? / I was wondering if I could …

**Ngữ pháp 2 – xin lỗi và đưa giải pháp**
• Báo tin xấu nhẹ nhàng: **I'm afraid** the room isn't ready yet.
• Xin lỗi: We're very sorry for the inconvenience. / I do apologise.
• Giải pháp bằng will (quyết định ngay): **I'll** move you to another room right away. / I'll send someone up to fix it.
• Khách phàn nàn lịch sự: I'm sorry to bother you, but … / There seems to be a problem with …

**Grammar 2 – apologising and offering a solution**
• Soften bad news: **I'm afraid** the room isn't ready yet.
• Apologise: We're very sorry for the inconvenience. / I do apologise.
• Solution with will (instant decision): **I'll** move you to another room right away. / I'll send someone up to fix it.
• Polite complaints: I'm sorry to bother you, but … / There seems to be a problem with …

**Phát âm – trọng âm từ dài**
• incon**VEN**ience /ˌɪn.kənˈviː.ni.əns/
• re**CEP**tion /rɪˈsep.ʃən/
• accommo**DA**tion /əˌkɑː.məˈdeɪ.ʃən/
• Quy tắc: từ đuôi -tion/-sion thường nhấn âm ngay trước đuôi: reserVAtion, compenSAtion.

**Pronunciation – stress in long words**
• incon**VEN**ience /ˌɪn.kənˈviː.ni.əns/
• re**CEP**tion /rɪˈsep.ʃən/
• accommo**DA**tion /əˌkɑː.məˈdeɪ.ʃən/
• Rule: words ending in -tion/-sion usually stress the syllable just before the ending: reserVAtion, compenSAtion.

**Tự luyện ngoài app**
• Nghe (25 phút): nghe 1 đoạn khách gọi điện khiếu nại, ghi lại vấn đề và cách nhân viên xử lý.
• Nói (30 phút): đóng vai lễ tân xử lý 3 tình huống: nhận phòng, phòng ồn, khách đòi hoàn tiền.
• Đọc (20 phút): đọc 5 đánh giá khách sạn trên mạng, phân loại khen / chê theo: phòng, vị trí, nhân viên, giá.
• Viết (35 phút): viết thư trả lời 1 đánh giá tiêu cực, 120 từ: cảm ơn, xin lỗi, giải pháp, mời quay lại.
• Từ vựng (15 phút): học 15 từ về tiện nghi phòng (air conditioning, towel, Wi-Fi, breakfast …).
• Thử thách (20 phút): đọc 10 đánh giá thật của một khách sạn bằng tiếng Anh, ghi 10 cụm từ hay dùng để khen và chê.

**Practice outside the app**
• Listening (25 min): listen to a guest phoning to complain; note the problem and how the staff handle it.
• Speaking (30 min): role-play a receptionist in 3 situations: check-in, a noisy room, a guest asking for a refund.
• Reading (20 min): read 5 online hotel reviews; sort praise and criticism by room, location, staff and price.
• Writing (35 min): reply to a negative review in 120 words: thank, apologise, offer a solution, invite the guest back.
• Vocabulary (15 min): learn 15 words for room facilities (air conditioning, towel, Wi-Fi, breakfast …).
• Challenge (20 min): read 10 real reviews of a hotel in English and note 10 phrases guests use to praise and complain.

Leave the bags and have a free coffee while waiting

e: I've = I have; “double room” hai từ riêng; “for two nights” chỉ khoảng thời gian.

warm.s: We'll move you to another room right away.
e: We'll = We will (quyết định/lời hứa ngay). “right away” = ngay lập tức.
We'll = We will (an instant promise). “right away” = immediately.

warm.s: Good customer service means listening patiently, solving problems quickly and making every guest feel that their comfort really matters to you.
e: Câu hỏi: What makes good customer service? – Gợi ý trả lời mẫu. Nhấn “patiently”, “quickly”, “matters”.
Question: What makes good customer service? – Model answer. Stress “patiently”, “quickly” and “matters”.

warm.s: Last year I stayed in a hotel where the shower was broken, and although I complained twice, nobody came to fix it until the next afternoon.
e: Câu hỏi: Tell me about a bad experience at a hotel or shop. – Gợi ý trả lời mẫu. Đọc rõ đuôi -ed: stayed /d/, complained /d/.
Question: Tell me about a bad experience at a hotel or shop. – Model answer. Pronounce the -ed endings: stayed /d/, complained /d/.

hard.s: Xin lỗi đã làm phiền, nhưng phòng bên cạnh ồn quá nên tôi không ngủ được – có cách nào đổi cho tôi phòng yên tĩnh hơn không?
a: Sorry to bother you, but the room next door is so noisy that I can't get to sleep – is there any way you could move me to a quieter room?
I'm sorry to bother you, but the room next door is so noisy that I can't sleep. Is there any chance you could move me to a quieter room?
Sorry to bother you, but the people next door are so noisy I can't get to sleep – would it be possible to move me to a quieter room?
e: “Sorry to bother you, but …” mở đầu lời phàn nàn lịch sự; “so … that” = quá … đến nỗi; “get to sleep” = ngủ được; “Is there any way you could …?” là yêu cầu mềm mỏng.
“Sorry to bother you, but …” opens a polite complaint; “so … that” shows result; “get to sleep” = manage to fall asleep; “Is there any way you could …?” is a soft request.
f: is there any way you could move me

q: Tường thuật lại lời lễ tân, bắt đầu bằng “The receptionist promised that …”.
Report the receptionist's words, starting with “The receptionist promised that …”.
hard.s: “We'll send someone up to fix the shower first thing tomorrow morning.”
a: The receptionist promised that they would send someone up to fix the shower first thing the next morning.
The receptionist promised that they would send someone up to fix the shower first thing the following morning.
The receptionist promised that they'd send someone up to fix the shower first thing the next morning.
e: Tường thuật: will → would, tomorrow morning → the next/following morning. “send someone up” = cho người lên phòng; “first thing” = việc đầu tiên, sớm nhất.
Reported speech: will → would, tomorrow morning → the next/following morning. “send someone up” = send a staff member to the room; “first thing” = very early.

hard.s: If I had known the pool was closed for repairs, I would book a different hotel, so I think a partial refund would be fair.
a: If I had known the pool was closed for repairs, I would have booked a different hotel, so I think a partial refund would be fair.
If I'd known the pool was closed for repairs, I'd have booked a different hotel, so I think a partial refund would be fair.
e: Câu điều kiện loại 3 (chuyện đã qua): If + had + V3, would have + V3 → would have booked.
Third conditional (past situation): If + had + past participle, would have + past participle → would have booked.

hard.s: The staff really went out of their ___ to help us when our flight was cancelled – they even found us a room at a sister hotel.
a: way
e: “go out of your way (to do sth)” = cố gắng hết sức, làm nhiều hơn mức cần thiết – cụm rất hay gặp trong đánh giá khách sạn.
“go out of your way (to do sth)” = make a special effort – very common in hotel reviews.

rd2.tx:
Receptionist: Good evening, welcome to the Riverside Hotel. How may I help you?
Guest: Hi, I've booked a double room for two nights under the name Nguyen.
Receptionist: Thank you, Mr Nguyen. May I see your passport, please? … Here is your key card. You're in Room 512, and breakfast is served on the first floor.
(Twenty minutes later, on the phone)
Guest: I'm sorry to bother you, but the air conditioning in my room isn't working, and the room is very noisy because it's right next to the lift.
Receptionist: I'm terribly sorry for the inconvenience. I'm afraid we're quite full tonight, but we still have one room with a sea view on the eighth floor. Would you like to move there? There's no extra charge.
Guest: That would be great, thank you.
Receptionist: Not at all. I'll send someone up to help you with your luggage right away, and we'd also like to offer you a free dinner in our restaurant to apologise. Is there anything else I can do for you?
Guest: No, that's perfect. You've been very helpful.
rd2.tr:
Lễ tân: Chào buổi tối, chào mừng quý khách đến khách sạn Riverside. Tôi có thể giúp gì cho quý khách?
Khách: Chào chị, tôi đã đặt một phòng đôi hai đêm dưới tên Nguyễn.
Lễ tân: Cảm ơn anh Nguyễn. Cho tôi xem hộ chiếu của anh được không ạ? … Đây là thẻ phòng của anh. Anh ở phòng 512, bữa sáng được phục vụ ở tầng một.
(Hai mươi phút sau, qua điện thoại)
Khách: Xin lỗi đã làm phiền, nhưng điều hòa trong phòng tôi không chạy, và phòng rất ồn vì nằm ngay cạnh thang máy.
Lễ tân: Tôi vô cùng xin lỗi vì sự bất tiện này. Tôi e là tối nay khách sạn khá kín phòng, nhưng chúng tôi vẫn còn một phòng hướng biển ở tầng tám. Anh có muốn chuyển sang đó không? Không phải trả thêm phí ạ.
Khách: Vậy thì tuyệt quá, cảm ơn chị.
Lễ tân: Không có gì ạ. Tôi sẽ cho người lên giúp anh mang hành lý ngay, và chúng tôi cũng xin mời anh một bữa tối miễn phí ở nhà hàng để xin lỗi. Tôi còn có thể giúp gì thêm cho anh không?
Khách: Không, vậy là hoàn hảo rồi. Chị đã giúp đỡ rất nhiều.

q: Phòng đầu tiên của khách có những vấn đề gì?
What was wrong with the guest's first room?
o: Điều hòa hỏng và ồn vì gần thang máy
The air conditioning didn't work and it was noisy near the lift
It didn't have a sea view
e: “the air conditioning in my room isn't working, and the room is very noisy because it's right next to the lift”. View biển là của phòng mới.
“the air conditioning in my room isn't working, and the room is very noisy because it's right next to the lift”. The sea view belongs to the new room.
f: the air conditioning in my room isn't working

q: Khách phải trả thêm bao nhiêu để chuyển sang phòng mới?
How much extra does the guest pay for the new room?
e: “There's no extra charge.” Bữa tối là miễn phí, khách sạn tặng để xin lỗi.
“There's no extra charge.” The dinner is free – a gift to apologise.

q: Lễ tân làm gì để xin lỗi ngoài việc đổi phòng?
Apart from changing the room, what does the receptionist offer?
o: Một bữa tối miễn phí ở nhà hàng
A free dinner in the restaurant
e: “we'd also like to offer you a free dinner in our restaurant to apologise”. Bài không nhắc đến hoàn tiền.
“we'd also like to offer you a free dinner in our restaurant to apologise”. No refund is mentioned.

ex2.s: Good afternoon and welcome to the Lotus Hotel. ___ I take your name, please, so that I can find your reservation?
a: May
Could
Can
e: “May I …?” là cách xin phép trang trọng nhất của lễ tân; “Could I …?” cũng lịch sự.
“May I …?” is the most formal way for staff to ask permission; “Could I …?” is also polite.

ex2.s: We have a free upgrade available tonight – would you ___ a room with a sea view on the top floor?
a: like
e: “Would you like + danh từ/to V?” = mời, đề nghị. Không nhầm với “Do you like …?” (hỏi sở thích).
“Would you like + noun/to-infinitive?” = an offer. Don't confuse it with “Do you like …?” (asking about preferences).

ex2.s: I'm ___ the room isn't ready yet, but you're welcome to wait in the lobby and enjoy a drink on the house.
a: afraid
e: “I'm afraid (that) …” = tôi e là – làm mềm tin xấu, không có nghĩa “sợ hãi” ở đây.
“I'm afraid (that) …” softens bad news; it does not mean “scared” here.

ex2.s: I'm sorry to hear about the noise, sir – I ___ speak to the guests next door and ask them to keep the volume down.
e: Quyết định ngay khi nghe khách phàn nàn → will (I'll). “be going to” dùng cho kế hoạch đã có trước.
A decision made while hearing the complaint → will (I'll). “be going to” is for plans made earlier.
f: I'll speak to the guests next door

ex2.s: We apologise for the inconvenience and we would like offering you a twenty percent discount on your next stay with us.
a: We apologise for the inconvenience and we would like to offer you a twenty percent discount on your next stay with us.
We apologise for the inconvenience and we'd like to offer you a twenty percent discount on your next stay with us.
e: “would like + to V”: would like to offer. Không dùng V-ing sau would like.
“would like + to-infinitive”: would like to offer. No -ing after would like.

q: Viết lại lời phàn nàn cho lịch sự hơn, bắt đầu bằng “I'm sorry to bother you, but …”.
Rewrite the complaint more politely, starting with “I'm sorry to bother you, but …”.
ex2.s: The Wi-Fi in my room doesn't work and I need to send an important email tonight.
a: I'm sorry to bother you, but the Wi-Fi in my room doesn't work and I need to send an important email tonight.
I'm sorry to bother you, but the Wi-Fi in my room doesn't seem to work and I need to send an important email tonight.
I'm sorry to bother you, but the Wi-Fi in my room isn't working and I need to send an important email tonight.
e: Thêm cụm mở đầu lịch sự; có thể làm mềm hơn bằng “doesn't seem to work”.
Add the polite opening; you can soften further with “doesn't seem to work”.
f: I'm sorry to bother you, but

ex2.s: Mấy giờ phải trả phòng?
a: What time is check-out?
What time is checkout?
What time do I have to check out?
What time do we need to check out?
e: “check-out” (danh từ, có gạch nối) – “check out” (động từ). Hỏi giờ: What time …?
“check-out” is the noun (with a hyphen); “check out” is the verb. Ask the time with What time …?

ex2.s: Điều hòa trong phòng tôi bị hỏng.

The air conditioning in my room is not working.
The air conditioning in my room is broken.
The air conditioner in my room isn't working.
e: Người bản xứ hay nói “isn't working” cho thiết bị hỏng. “air conditioning” = hệ thống điều hòa; “air conditioner” = cái máy.
Native speakers often say “isn't working” for broken equipment. “air conditioning” = the system; “air conditioner” = the machine.

ex2.s: Chúng tôi rất tiếc vì phòng của quý khách chưa sẵn sàng, nhưng quý khách có thể gửi hành lý ở quầy lễ tân và đi dạo trong lúc chờ.
a: We're very sorry that your room isn't ready yet, but you can leave your luggage at reception and go for a walk while you wait.
We are very sorry that your room is not ready yet, but you're welcome to leave your luggage at reception and go for a walk while you wait.
We're very sorry your room isn't ready yet, but you can leave your bags at reception and take a walk while you wait.
e: “sorry that + mệnh đề”; “luggage” không đếm được (không thêm -s); “while you wait” = trong lúc chờ.
“sorry that + clause”; “luggage” is uncountable (no -s); “while you wait” = during the waiting time.

ex2.s: If you are not|completely satisfied|with your room,|please let us know|and we will do|our best|to find a solution
m: Nếu quý khách chưa hoàn toàn hài lòng với phòng, xin hãy cho chúng tôi biết và chúng tôi sẽ cố gắng hết sức tìm giải pháp.

“satisfied with”; “let us know” = tell us; “do our best to” = try as hard as we can.

q: Viết email khiếu nại khoảng 120 từ gửi khách sạn: mô tả 2 vấn đề, ảnh hưởng, yêu cầu cụ thể (hoàn tiền một phần, đổi phòng).
Write a complaint email to a hotel (about 120 words): describe 2 problems, their effect and a specific request (partial refund, room change).
ex2.m:
Subject: Complaint about my stay, reservation no. 4572

Dear Sir or Madam,

I stayed at your hotel from 3 to 5 August in a double room with a sea view. Unfortunately, I was disappointed with my stay for two reasons.

First, the air conditioning in my room did not work, and although I reported the problem twice, nobody came to repair it. Second, the room was extremely noisy because it was next to the kitchen, so my wife and I hardly slept.

As a result, we felt exhausted during our holiday. I would therefore be grateful if you could offer us a partial refund of one night.

I look forward to your reply.

Yours faithfully,
Le Van Hung
e: Cần có: thông tin đặt phòng (ngày, số đặt chỗ); 2 vấn đề cụ thể; ảnh hưởng đến bạn; yêu cầu rõ ràng và lịch sự (I would be grateful if …).
Include: booking details (dates, reference); 2 specific problems; the effect on you; a clear, polite request (I would be grateful if …).

th:
**Ngữ pháp 1 – Thì kể chuyện: quá khứ hoàn thành & bị động quá khứ**
• **had + V3**: việc xảy ra TRƯỚC một mốc quá khứ: By the time we arrived, the exhibition **had closed**.
• Bị động quá khứ: **was/were + V3**: Construction **was begun** in 1804. / The palace **was decorated** with poems.
• Bị động quá khứ hoàn thành: **had been + V3**: Many buildings **had been damaged** before restoration began.
• Hiện tại hoàn thành bị động cho kết quả đến nay: Many buildings **have been restored** since 1993.

**Grammar 1 – Narrative tenses: past perfect & past passive**
• **had + past participle**: an action BEFORE a past point: By the time we arrived, the exhibition **had closed**.
• Past passive: **was/were + past participle**: The palace **was decorated** with poems.
• Past perfect passive: **had been + past participle**: Many buildings **had been damaged** before restoration began.
• Present perfect passive for results up to now: Many buildings **have been restored** since 1993.

**Ngữ pháp 2 – used to & would cho thói quen quá khứ**
• **used to + V**: thói quen VÀ trạng thái quá khứ: The city **used to be** the capital.
• **would + V**: chỉ cho hành động lặp lại, không dùng cho trạng thái: Emperors **would hold** ceremonies here.
• Sai: “The city would be the capital.” (trạng thái → phải dùng used to).

**Grammar 2 – used to & would for past habits**
• **used to + verb**: past habits AND states: The city **used to be** the capital.
• **would + verb**: repeated actions only, never states: Emperors **would hold** ceremonies here.
• Wrong: “The city would be the capital.” (a state → use used to).

**Phát âm – Trọng âm thay đổi theo họ từ**
• **HIS**tory – his**TOR**ic – his**TOR**ian
• **PHO**tograph – pho**TOG**rapher – photo**GRAPH**ic
• **AR**chitect – **AR**chitecture – archi**TEC**tural
• **AR**tist – ar**TIS**tic; **CEN**tury; **HER**itage /ˈher.ɪ.t̬ɪdʒ/.
• Mẹo: đuôi **-ic, -ian, -ical** kéo trọng âm về âm tiết ngay trước nó.

**Pronunciation – Stress shifts in word families**
• **HIS**tory – his**TOR**ic – his**TOR**ian
• **PHO**tograph – pho**TOG**rapher – photo**GRAPH**ic
• **AR**chitect – **AR**chitecture – archi**TEC**tural
• **AR**tist – ar**TIS**tic; **CEN**tury; **HER**itage /ˈher.ɪ.t̬ɪdʒ/.
• Tip: endings **-ic, -ian, -ical** pull the stress to the syllable just before them.

**Tự luyện ngoài app**
• Nghe (25 phút): nghe 1 audio guide bảo tàng (trên website bảo tàng lớn), ghi lại các mốc năm và động từ bị động.
• Nói (25 phút): làm “hướng dẫn viên” 2 phút giới thiệu 1 di tích ở quê bạn.
• Đọc (25 phút): đọc 1 bài về lịch sử một công trình nổi tiếng, vẽ dòng thời gian.
• Viết (35 phút): viết 120–150 từ mô tả 1 bức tranh hoặc di tích, dùng quá khứ hoàn thành.
• Từ vựng (15 phút): học họ từ: history/historic/historical, art/artist/artistic/artwork.

**Practice outside the app**
• Listening (25 min): listen to a museum audio guide (on a major museum's website) and note dates and passive verbs.
• Speaking (25 min): be a “tour guide” for 2 minutes presenting a historic site in your hometown.
• Reading (25 min): read an article on the history of a famous building and draw a timeline.
• Writing (35 min): write 120–150 words describing a painting or monument, using the past perfect.
• Vocabulary (15 min): learn word families: history/historic/historical, art/artist/artistic/artwork.

warm.s: By the time the museum opened to the public, experts had spent five years restoring the damaged paintings.
e: Quá khứ hoàn thành **had spent** (trước mốc “opened”); **spend + thời gian + V-ing**.
Past perfect **had spent** (before “opened”); **spend + time + -ing**.

warm.s: Although I'm not an artistic person, I find historical places fascinating because every building has a story to tell.
e: Chú ý trọng âm: ar**TIS**tic, his**TOR**ical, **FAS**cinating.

warm.s: When I was a child, my grandmother would take me to the old citadel every Sunday and tell me stories about the emperors.
e: “would take” = thói quen trong quá khứ; nối âm “take‿me”, “tell‿me”. **EM**peror nhấn âm đầu.

hard.s: Nói thật, tranh trừu tượng mình xem chẳng hiểu gì cả, nhưng mình vẫn thích đi bảo tàng cho vui.

To be honest, abstract art goes over my head, but I still enjoy going to museums for fun.

e: “xem chẳng hiểu gì” = **go (right) over my head** hoặc **can't make head or tail of** – thành ngữ tự nhiên trong hội thoại.
“not understand at all” = **go (right) over my head** or **can't make head or tail of** – natural idioms in conversation.

q: Viết lại thành câu điều kiện hỗn hợp: bắt đầu bằng “If we had…”.
Rewrite as a mixed conditional starting with “If we had…”.
hard.s: We didn't book the guided tour, and that's why we're so confused about these paintings now.
a: If we had booked the guided tour, we wouldn't be so confused about these paintings now.
If we had booked the guided tour, we would not be so confused about these paintings now.
If we'd booked the guided tour, we wouldn't be so confused about these paintings now.
e: Điều kiện hỗn hợp: nguyên nhân trong quá khứ (**had booked**) → kết quả ở hiện tại (**wouldn't be … now**).
Mixed conditional: a past cause (**had booked**) → a present result (**wouldn't be … now**).
f: If we had booked … we wouldn't be

hard.s: It's high time the city council renovate that old theatre – the roof has been leaking for years and the paint is peeling everywhere.
a: It's high time the city council renovated that old theatre – the roof has been leaking for years and the paint is peeling everywhere.
It is high time the city council renovated that old theatre – the roof has been leaking for years and the paint is peeling everywhere.
e: **It's (high) time + chủ ngữ + quá khứ đơn** để nói “đã đến lúc phải…”: renovated, không phải renovate.
**It's (high) time + subject + past simple** to say something should already happen: renovated, not renovate.
f: It's high time the city council renovated

hard.s: Honestly, I wasn't expecting much from the exhibition, but the last room, full of huge paintings of the sea, absolutely ___ me away.
a: blew
e: **blow sb away** (quá khứ: blew) = làm ai choáng ngợp, cực kỳ ấn tượng – cách khen rất tự nhiên.
**blow someone away** (past: blew) = impress someone enormously – a very natural way to praise something.

rd2.tx: Visitors who walk through the Imperial City in Hue today often find it hard to imagine how it looked two centuries ago. Construction began in 1804, shortly after Emperor Gia Long had united the country, and Hue remained the capital of Vietnam until 1945. Inside its thick walls, emperors would hold ceremonies, receive foreign envoys and study with court scholars. Many of the palaces were decorated with poems carved into wood and colourful ceramic mosaics. Sadly, a large part of the complex was destroyed during the war, especially in 1968, and by the time serious restoration began, many surviving buildings had also been damaged by storms and decades of neglect. In 1993, the Complex of Hue Monuments was recognised by UNESCO as a World Heritage Site, and since then dozens of buildings have been carefully restored. It is a slow process, because experts must study old photographs and records before a single roof tile is replaced. Even so, walking past the restored gates at sunset, you can easily understand why so many artists have been inspired by this place.
rd2.tr: Du khách dạo bước qua Hoàng thành Huế ngày nay thường khó hình dung nơi này trông thế nào hai thế kỷ trước. Việc xây dựng bắt đầu năm 1804, ngay sau khi vua Gia Long thống nhất đất nước, và Huế là kinh đô của Việt Nam cho đến năm 1945. Bên trong những bức tường dày, các hoàng đế thường cử hành nghi lễ, tiếp sứ thần nước ngoài và học tập cùng các học sĩ trong triều. Nhiều cung điện được trang trí bằng thơ khắc trên gỗ và những mảng khảm sành sứ đầy màu sắc. Đáng buồn là một phần lớn quần thể đã bị phá hủy trong chiến tranh, đặc biệt vào năm 1968, và đến khi việc trùng tu nghiêm túc bắt đầu thì nhiều công trình còn sót lại cũng đã bị bão và hàng chục năm bỏ bê làm hư hại. Năm 1993, Quần thể di tích Cố đô Huế được UNESCO công nhận là Di sản Thế giới, và kể từ đó hàng chục công trình đã được trùng tu cẩn thận. Đó là một quá trình chậm, vì các chuyên gia phải nghiên cứu ảnh cũ và tư liệu trước khi thay dù chỉ một viên ngói. Dù vậy, đi ngang qua những cổng thành đã được phục dựng lúc hoàng hôn, bạn sẽ dễ dàng hiểu vì sao rất nhiều nghệ sĩ đã lấy cảm hứng từ nơi này.

When did construction of the Imperial City begin?

In 1804, after the country had been united
e: “Construction began in 1804, shortly after Emperor Gia Long had united the country”. 1945 là năm Huế thôi làm kinh đô; 1993 là năm được UNESCO công nhận.
“Construction began in 1804, shortly after Emperor Gia Long had united the country”. 1945 is when Hue stopped being the capital; 1993 is the UNESCO year.

Lượng khách du lịch quá đông
e: “many surviving buildings had also been damaged by storms and decades of neglect” – bị động quá khứ hoàn thành.
“many surviving buildings had also been damaged by storms and decades of neglect” – past perfect passive.

ex2.s: By the time we finally got to the gallery, the most famous painting ___ to another museum for a special exhibition, so we only saw a poster of it.
e: Việc chuyển tranh xảy ra TRƯỚC lúc “we got to the gallery” và bức tranh bị chuyển → **had been moved** (bị động quá khứ hoàn thành).
The painting was moved BEFORE “we got to the gallery” and it received the action → **had been moved** (past perfect passive).

ex2.s: When my grandfather was a young man, he ___ spend every Sunday morning sitting by the Perfume River and drawing the boats that passed by.
a: would
used to
e: Hành động lặp lại trong quá khứ → **would** hoặc **used to** + V nguyên mẫu đều đúng.
A repeated past action → **would** or **used to** + base verb are both correct.

ex2.s: The pagoda, which was first built in the eleventh century, was badly damaged by a fire in 1950 and had rebuilt twice since then.
a: The pagoda, which was first built in the eleventh century, was badly damaged by a fire in 1950 and has been rebuilt twice since then.
The pagoda, which was first built in the eleventh century, was badly damaged by a fire in 1950 and has been rebuilt twice since.
e: “since then” (từ đó đến nay) → hiện tại hoàn thành; ngôi chùa được xây lại → bị động: **has been rebuilt**.
“since then” (until now) needs the present perfect, and the pagoda receives the action → passive: **has been rebuilt**.
f: has been rebuilt twice since then

ex2.s: Before the museum reopened last spring, a team of experts had spent five years to restore the damaged paintings one by one.
a: Before the museum reopened last spring, a team of experts had spent five years restoring the damaged paintings one by one.
e: Cấu trúc **spend + thời gian + V-ing**, không dùng “to + V”.
The pattern is **spend + time + -ing**, not “to + verb”.

ex2.s: Ngôi đền này được xây dựng hơn tám trăm năm trước và đã được trùng tu nhiều lần.
a: This temple was built more than eight hundred years ago and has been restored many times.
This temple was built over eight hundred years ago and has been restored many times.
This temple was built more than 800 years ago and has been restored several times.
This temple was built more than eight hundred years ago and has been renovated many times.
e: “được xây … năm trước” → bị động quá khứ **was built … ago**; “đã được trùng tu nhiều lần” (đến nay) → **has been restored**.
“was built … ago” is past simple passive; “has been restored many times” is present perfect passive (up to now).

ex2.s: Khi chúng tôi đến nơi thì buổi triển lãm đã đóng cửa, nên chúng tôi đành đi dạo quanh hồ.
a: When we arrived, the exhibition had already closed, so we went for a walk around the lake instead.
When we got there, the exhibition had already closed, so we walked around the lake instead.
By the time we arrived, the exhibition had already closed, so we went for a walk around the lake instead.
When we arrived, the exhibition had closed, so we had to walk around the lake instead.
e: Triển lãm đóng TRƯỚC khi chúng tôi đến → **had (already) closed**. “đành” có thể dịch bằng **instead** hoặc **had to**.
The exhibition closed BEFORE we arrived → **had (already) closed**. “đành” can be rendered with **instead** or **had to**.

q: Viết lại câu ở thể bị động, bắt đầu bằng “These wooden panels…”.
Rewrite the sentence in the passive, starting with “These wooden panels…”.
ex2.s: Local craftsmen carved these wooden panels by hand more than a century ago.
a: These wooden panels were carved by hand by local craftsmen more than a century ago.
These wooden panels were carved by local craftsmen by hand more than a century ago.
These wooden panels were hand-carved by local craftsmen more than a century ago.
e: Quá khứ đơn bị động: **were carved**. Giữ “by local craftsmen” vì người làm là thông tin quan trọng.
Past simple passive: **were carved**. Keep “by local craftsmen” because who did it is important here.

ex2.s: By the time|the archaeologists|arrived,|local farmers|had already found|hundreds of|ancient coins|in the rice field.
m: Khi các nhà khảo cổ đến nơi, nông dân địa phương đã tìm thấy hàng trăm đồng xu cổ trên ruộng lúa.
By the time the archaeologists arrived, local farmers had already found hundreds of ancient coins in the rice field.
e: **By the time + quá khứ đơn**, mệnh đề chính dùng **quá khứ hoàn thành** (had already found).
**By the time + past simple**, then the main clause uses the **past perfect** (had already found).

q: Viết 100–120 từ mô tả một di tích lịch sử bạn từng đến: được xây khi nào, từng dùng làm gì, đã thay đổi ra sao, cảm nhận của bạn.
Write 100–120 words describing a historic site you have visited: when it was built, what it was used for, how it has changed and how you felt.
ex2.m: Last summer I visited the Temple of Literature in Hanoi, which was founded in 1070 and later became Vietnam's first national university. For centuries, students would come here from all over the country to prepare for the royal exams. The names of the successful candidates were carved on stone stelae, which still stand on the backs of stone turtles. By the time I arrived, the morning crowds had already left, so the courtyards were surprisingly peaceful. Some buildings have been restored, but the atmosphere still feels ancient. Standing among the old trees, I could easily imagine nervous young scholars waiting for their results.
e: Cần có: ít nhất 2 câu bị động quá khứ; 1 câu quá khứ hoàn thành; would/used to cho thói quen quá khứ; 1 câu hiện tại hoàn thành bị động và cảm nhận cá nhân.
Include: at least 2 past passive sentences; one past perfect; would/used to for past habits; one present perfect passive and a personal reaction.

t: Sức khỏe tinh thần & lối sống
th:
**Ngữ pháp 1 – Lời khuyên & hối tiếc với động từ khuyết thiếu**
• **should / ought to + V**: lời khuyên: You **should** take more breaks. / You **ought to** see a doctor.
• **had better (not) + V**: lời khuyên mạnh, có ý cảnh báo: You**'d better not** skip meals.
• **should have + V3**: lẽ ra nên làm (nhưng đã không làm): I **should have said** no.
• **shouldn't have + V3**: lẽ ra không nên làm: I **shouldn't have stayed** up so late.
• Sau should/had better KHÔNG có “to”: ~~should to try~~.

**Grammar 1 – Advice & regret with modals**
• **should / ought to + verb**: advice: You **should** take more breaks. / You **ought to** see a doctor.
• **had better (not) + verb**: strong advice with a warning: You**'d better not** skip meals.
• **should have + past participle**: it was a good idea but you didn't do it: I **should have said** no.
• **shouldn't have + past participle**: you did it but it was a mistake: I **shouldn't have stayed** up so late.
• No “to” after should / had better: ~~should to try~~.

**Ngữ pháp 2 – Động từ đổi nghĩa với to-V / V-ing**
• **stop doing**: ngừng làm: Stop checking emails at night. ↔ **stop to do**: dừng lại để làm: I stopped to rest.
• **try to do**: cố gắng: Try to sleep eight hours. ↔ **try doing**: thử làm (xem có hiệu quả không): Try drinking herbal tea.
• **remember to do**: nhớ phải làm (tương lai) ↔ **remember doing**: nhớ đã làm (quá khứ).

**Grammar 2 – Verbs that change meaning with to-infinitive / -ing**
• **stop doing**: quit an activity: Stop checking emails at night. ↔ **stop to do**: stop in order to do: I stopped to rest.
• **try to do**: make an effort: Try to sleep eight hours. ↔ **try doing**: experiment: Try drinking herbal tea.
• **remember to do**: not forget a future task ↔ **remember doing**: recall a past action.

Dear Minh,
Thank you for your honest message. You say that since starting your new job you have been sleeping badly, skipping meals and feeling anxious every Sunday evening. First of all, you are not alone: many young professionals go through exactly the same thing. Looking back, you probably should have said no when your manager asked you to take on a second project, but it is not too late to set clearer boundaries. Try to stop checking work emails after eight o'clock, and remember to take short breaks during the day – even a ten-minute walk can lower stress. You had better not rely on coffee and energy drinks to keep going, because they will only make your sleep worse. It might also be worth talking to a friend or family member about how you feel; bottling up your emotions rarely helps. Finally, if the anxiety doesn't go away after a few weeks, you ought to see a doctor or a counsellor. Asking for help is a sign of strength, not weakness.
Take care,
Anna

**Ngữ pháp 1 – Bị động với động từ tường thuật**
• **It is said / believed / thought / estimated that** + mệnh đề: **It is believed that** new medicines will be needed.
• **Chủ ngữ + is said / believed + to V** (hiện tại): The drug **is thought to be** safe.
• **Chủ ngữ + is said + to have + V3** (quá khứ): Penicillin **is estimated to have saved** millions of lives. / The wheel **is thought to have been invented** in Mesopotamia.
• Dùng trong văn khoa học/tin tức để nói một cách khách quan, thận trọng.

**Grammar 1 – Passive reporting structures**
• **It is said / believed / thought / estimated that** + clause: **It is believed that** new medicines will be needed.
• **Subject + is said / believed + to + verb** (present): The drug **is thought to be** safe.
• **Subject + is said + to have + past participle** (past): Penicillin **is estimated to have saved** millions of lives. / The wheel **is thought to have been invented** in Mesopotamia.
• Used in science writing and news to sound objective and careful.

**Ngữ pháp 2 – Bị động ở các thì**
• Hiện tại hoàn thành: **have/has been + V3**: Many landlines **have been replaced** by smartphones.
• Tiếp diễn: **is/are being + V3**: Antibiotics **are being used** too often.
• Với động từ khuyết thiếu: **will have to be + V3**: New drugs **will have to be developed**.
• “It was not until … that …” = mãi đến … mới …: It was not until the 1940s that penicillin was mass-produced.

**Grammar 2 – The passive in different tenses**
• Present perfect: **have/has been + past participle**: Many landlines **have been replaced** by smartphones.
• Continuous: **is/are being + past participle**: Antibiotics **are being used** too often.
• With modals: **will have to be + past participle**: New drugs **will have to be developed**.
• “It was not until … that …” = only at that time: It was not until the 1940s that penicillin was mass-produced.

I'm not very tech-savvy – could you show me how to connect this printer to my laptop again?
I'm not very good with technology – could you show me again how to connect this printer to my laptop?
I'm not very tech-savvy, so could you show me again how to connect this printer to my laptop?
e: “rành công nghệ” = **tech-savvy** (thân mật). “chỉ cho mình cách” = **show me how to + V**.
“good with technology” = **tech-savvy** (informal). “chỉ cho mình cách” = **show me how to + verb**.

q: Viết lại câu dùng “… is supposed to have been …”.
Rewrite the sentence using “… is supposed to have been …”.
hard.s: People say that someone invented this gadget by accident in their garage.
a: This gadget is supposed to have been invented by accident in someone's garage.
This gadget is supposed to have been invented by accident in a garage.
e: **be supposed to have been + V3** = nghe nói là đã được… (thân mật hơn “is said to”, hay dùng khi kể chuyện).
**be supposed to have been + past participle** = people say it was… (more informal than “is said to”, common in chat).
f: is supposed to have been invented

hard.s: My laptop keeps freezing whenever I open more than two apps, so I'm going to get it repair before the warranty runs out next month.
a: My laptop keeps freezing whenever I open more than two apps, so I'm going to get it repaired before the warranty runs out next month.
My laptop keeps freezing whenever I open more than two apps, so I'm going to have it repaired before the warranty runs out next month.
e: Thể nhờ/sai khiến: **get/have + vật + V3** (nhờ người khác làm): get it **repaired**.
Causative: **get/have + object + past participle** (someone else does it): get it **repaired**.

hard.s: Honestly, all these smart home gadgets are a bit lost ___ me – I just want a kettle that boils water without asking me to update it first!
a: on
e: **be lost on sb** = ai đó không hiểu/không thấy giá trị của điều gì. Giới từ cố định là **on**.
**be lost on someone** = they don't understand or appreciate it. The fixed preposition is **on**.

rd2.tx: Some of the most important inventions in history were discovered by accident. In 1928, the Scottish scientist Alexander Fleming returned from a holiday and noticed that mould had grown on one of the dishes he had left in his laboratory. Surprisingly, the bacteria around the mould had been killed. Fleming realised that the mould was producing a substance that could destroy bacteria, and he called it penicillin. However, it was not until the early 1940s that a team at the University of Oxford found a way to produce the drug in large quantities. Since then, penicillin and the antibiotics that were developed after it are estimated to have saved millions of lives. Today, doctors warn that antibiotics are being used too often, and many bacteria have become resistant to them. It is believed that new medicines will have to be developed in the coming decades. Fleming's story is often used to show that curiosity matters as much as careful planning: if he had thrown the dirty dish away, the world might have waited much longer for this life-saving discovery.
rd2.tr: Một số phát minh quan trọng nhất trong lịch sử được phát hiện một cách tình cờ. Năm 1928, nhà khoa học người Scotland Alexander Fleming đi nghỉ về và nhận thấy nấm mốc đã mọc trên một trong những chiếc đĩa ông để lại trong phòng thí nghiệm. Thật bất ngờ, vi khuẩn xung quanh vết mốc đã bị tiêu diệt. Fleming nhận ra rằng nấm mốc đang tiết ra một chất có thể tiêu diệt vi khuẩn, và ông gọi nó là penicillin. Tuy nhiên, mãi đến đầu những năm 1940, một nhóm tại Đại học Oxford mới tìm ra cách sản xuất loại thuốc này với số lượng lớn. Kể từ đó, penicillin và các loại kháng sinh được phát triển sau nó ước tính đã cứu sống hàng triệu người. Ngày nay, các bác sĩ cảnh báo rằng kháng sinh đang bị sử dụng quá thường xuyên, và nhiều loại vi khuẩn đã trở nên kháng thuốc. Người ta tin rằng các loại thuốc mới sẽ phải được phát triển trong những thập kỷ tới. Câu chuyện của Fleming thường được dùng để cho thấy sự tò mò cũng quan trọng như việc lên kế hoạch cẩn thận: nếu ông đã vứt chiếc đĩa bẩn đi, thế giới có lẽ đã phải chờ lâu hơn nhiều cho khám phá cứu người này.

q: Fleming nhận thấy điều gì khi đi nghỉ về?
What did Fleming notice when he returned from holiday?
o: Vi khuẩn quanh vết mốc đã bị tiêu diệt
The bacteria around the mould had been killed
e: “mould had grown on one of the dishes… the bacteria around the mould had been killed” – bị động quá khứ hoàn thành.
“mould had grown on one of the dishes… the bacteria around the mould had been killed” – past perfect passive.
f: the bacteria around the mould had been killed

q: Ai tìm ra cách sản xuất penicillin số lượng lớn?
Who found a way to produce penicillin in large quantities?
o: Một nhóm ở Đại học Oxford
A team at the University of Oxford
e: “it was not until the early 1940s that a team at the University of Oxford found a way to produce the drug in large quantities” – mãi đến đầu thập niên 1940 mới làm được.
“it was not until the early 1940s that a team at the University of Oxford found a way…” – this only happened in the early 1940s.
f: a team at the University of Oxford

q: Các bác sĩ ngày nay cảnh báo điều gì?
What do doctors warn about today?
o: Kháng sinh bị dùng quá nhiều và vi khuẩn kháng thuốc
Antibiotics are overused and bacteria have become resistant
Penicillin không còn được sản xuất
Nấm mốc trong nhà rất nguy hiểm
Mould at home is very dangerous
e: “antibiotics are being used too often, and many bacteria have become resistant to them”.
“antibiotics are being used too often, and many bacteria have become resistant to them”.

ex2.s: It ___ that the first computers were so large and heavy that a single machine could fill an entire room in a university building.
e: Cấu trúc bị động tường thuật: **It is said that…** (người ta nói rằng). “It says” chỉ dùng cho văn bản (The sign says…).
Passive reporting: **It is said that…**. “It says” is only for texts (The sign says…).

ex2.s: Over the past twenty years, millions of old landline telephones ___ (replace) by smartphones, which are cheaper, smaller and far more useful.
a: have been replaced
e: “Over the past twenty years” → hiện tại hoàn thành; điện thoại bị thay → bị động: **have been replaced**.
“Over the past twenty years” → present perfect; the phones receive the action → passive: **have been replaced**.

ex2.s: The telephone is believed to invent by Alexander Graham Bell in 1876, although several other inventors were working on similar ideas at that time.
a: The telephone is believed to have been invented by Alexander Graham Bell in 1876, although several other inventors were working on similar ideas at that time.
e: Việc trong quá khứ + chủ ngữ bị tác động → **is believed to have been + V3**: to have been invented.
A past action done to the subject → **is believed to have been + past participle**: to have been invented.
f: is believed to have been invented

ex2.s: The results of the experiment was checked by three different laboratories before they were finally published in a well-known scientific journal.
a: The results of the experiment were checked by three different laboratories before they were finally published in a well-known scientific journal.
e: Chủ ngữ thật là **results** (số nhiều) → **were checked**. Đừng để “experiment” số ít đánh lừa.
The real subject is **results** (plural) → **were checked**. Don't be misled by the singular “experiment”.

ex2.s: Người ta tin rằng loại vắc-xin mới này sẽ cứu sống hàng nghìn người mỗi năm ở những nước nghèo, nơi căn bệnh này vẫn còn phổ biến.
a: It is believed that this new vaccine will save thousands of lives every year in poor countries, where the disease is still common.
It's believed that this new vaccine will save thousands of lives every year in poor countries, where the disease is still common.
This new vaccine is believed to save thousands of lives each year in poor countries, where the disease is still common.
It is believed that this new vaccine will save thousands of people every year in poorer countries, where the disease is still common.
e: “Người ta tin rằng” = **It is believed that**. “nơi” = **where** (mệnh đề quan hệ không xác định, có dấu phẩy).
“Người ta tin rằng” = **It is believed that**. “nơi” = **where** (a non-defining clause, with a comma).

ex2.s: Kể từ khi Internet được phát minh, cách chúng ta học tập và làm việc đã thay đổi hoàn toàn, và ngày càng nhiều người làm việc tại nhà.
a: Since the Internet was invented, the way we study and work has changed completely, and more and more people work from home.
Since the Internet was invented, the way we study and work has completely changed, and more and more people are working from home.
Since the invention of the Internet, the way we learn and work has changed completely, and more and more people work from home.
Since the Internet was invented, the way we study and work has changed completely, and more and more people now work from home.
e: “Kể từ khi” + quá khứ đơn bị động (**was invented**), mệnh đề chính hiện tại hoàn thành (**has changed**). Chủ ngữ “the way” số ít → has.
“Since” + past simple passive (**was invented**), main clause in the present perfect (**has changed**). “the way” is singular → has.

q: Viết lại câu ở thể bị động (bắt đầu bằng “A new type of battery…”).
Rewrite the sentence in the passive (start with “A new type of battery…”).
ex2.s: Scientists at a Korean university have developed a new type of battery that can be charged in five minutes.
a: A new type of battery that can be charged in five minutes has been developed by scientists at a Korean university.
A new type of battery that can be charged in five minutes has been developed at a Korean university.
e: Hiện tại hoàn thành bị động: **has been developed** (chủ ngữ “A new type” số ít).
Present perfect passive: **has been developed** (the subject “A new type” is singular).

ex2.s: It was not until|the early 1940s|that|penicillin|could be produced|in large enough quantities|to treat|soldiers and ordinary patients.
m: Mãi đến đầu những năm 1940, penicillin mới có thể được sản xuất đủ nhiều để điều trị cho binh lính và bệnh nhân bình thường.
It was not until the early 1940s that penicillin could be produced in large enough quantities to treat soldiers and ordinary patients.
e: **It was not until + thời gian + that…** = mãi đến … mới …; “large enough quantities” – enough đứng sau tính từ.
**It was not until + time + that…** = only then; “large enough quantities” – enough goes after the adjective.

q: Viết 100–120 từ về một phát minh đã thay đổi cuộc sống của bạn: nó là gì, được phát minh khi nào, đã thay đổi thói quen của bạn ra sao.
Write 100–120 words about an invention that has changed your life: what it is, when it was invented and how it has changed your habits.
ex2.m: For me, the most important invention is the smartphone. Mobile phones had been around for years, but the first modern touch-screen smartphones were introduced in 2007, and they have changed almost every part of my day. I use mine to study English, pay for coffee and find my way around new cities. It is often said that smartphones make us less sociable, and I think that is partly true: I have been known to check messages during family dinners! However, without my phone I would never have kept in touch with my friends abroad. It is a tool, and it should be used wisely.
e: Cần có: ít nhất 2 câu bị động (was introduced, has been…); 1 cấu trúc tường thuật bị động (It is said that / is thought to); ví dụ cụ thể về thói quen; ý kiến cân bằng (lợi & hại).
Include: at least 2 passive sentences (was introduced, has been…); one passive reporting structure (It is said that / is thought to); concrete examples of habits; a balanced opinion (pros and cons).

t: Bài đọc: Làm việc từ xa

rd.tx: Since 2020, millions of office workers have discovered what it is like to work from home. For many, the benefits were obvious: no commuting, more flexible hours and more time with family. Some companies even reported that productivity had increased. However, the picture is more complicated than it first appears. Junior employees, in particular, often say they miss the informal learning that happens when you sit next to experienced colleagues. Others find it hard to switch off, because their bedroom has become their office. As a result, many firms have adopted a hybrid model, asking staff to come in two or three days a week. Whether this compromise will last remains to be seen, but it is unlikely that working life will ever return completely to the way it was before.
rd.tr: Từ năm 2020, hàng triệu nhân viên văn phòng đã biết làm việc ở nhà là như thế nào. Với nhiều người, lợi ích rất rõ: không phải đi lại, giờ giấc linh hoạt và có thêm thời gian cho gia đình. Một số công ty còn báo cáo năng suất tăng. Tuy nhiên, bức tranh phức tạp hơn vẻ ngoài. Đặc biệt, nhân viên trẻ thường nói họ nhớ việc học hỏi không chính thức khi ngồi cạnh đồng nghiệp giàu kinh nghiệm. Người khác thấy khó “tắt” khỏi công việc vì phòng ngủ đã thành văn phòng. Vì vậy, nhiều công ty chuyển sang mô hình kết hợp, yêu cầu nhân viên lên văn phòng hai hoặc ba ngày mỗi tuần. Giải pháp dung hòa này có bền vững không thì còn phải chờ xem, nhưng khó có khả năng đời sống công sở sẽ quay lại hoàn toàn như trước.

ex: Who most often misses informal learning?
vài ngày ở văn phòng, vài ngày ở nhà
some days in the office, some at home
Quan điểm của tác giả về tương lai?
The writer's view of the future?
chắc chắn quay lại như cũ
work will fully return to normal
khó quay lại hoàn toàn như trước
unlikely to fully return to how it was
làm việc tại nhà sẽ biến mất
___ this compromise will last remains to be seen.

warm.s: Many firms have adopted a hybrid model, asking their staff to come into the office two or three days a week and work from home the rest of the time.
q: “Mô hình kết hợp” là gì?
What is the hybrid model?
o: Lên văn phòng 2–3 ngày, còn lại làm ở nhà
Office two or three days, home the rest
Luôn làm việc ở văn phòng
e: Cụm phân từ “asking their staff to come into the office two or three days a week” giải thích hybrid model chính là sự kết hợp hai nơi làm việc.
The participle clause “asking their staff to come into the office two or three days a week” explains that the hybrid model combines both places.

warm.s: Junior employees often say that they miss the informal learning that happens when you sit next to experienced colleagues.
e: Hai chữ that có hai vai trò: that thứ nhất mở đầu mệnh đề tường thuật, that thứ hai là đại từ quan hệ thay cho “the informal learning”.
The two thats have different jobs: the first introduces reported speech, the second is a relative pronoun for “the informal learning”.

warm.s: Whether this compromise will last remains to be seen, but working life is unlikely to return completely to the way it was.
e: Chủ ngữ là cả mệnh đề “Whether this compromise will last”; ngắt hơi trước “remains”. Nhấn vào “unlikely” và “completely”.
The subject is the whole clause “Whether this compromise will last”; pause before “remains”. Stress “unlikely” and “completely”.

ex2.s: Since my bedroom became my office during the pandemic, I have found it very hard to ___ in the evening and stop checking my email.
e: switch off (nghĩa bóng) = thôi nghĩ về công việc, thư giãn – đúng như trong bài đọc. turn down = từ chối/vặn nhỏ; give up = bỏ cuộc.
switch off (figurative) = stop thinking about work and relax, as in the passage. turn down = refuse/lower; give up = quit.

ex2.s: Whether the four-day working week will become common in Vietnam ___ to be seen, but several companies are already testing the idea.
a: remains
e: Thành ngữ “remains to be seen” = còn phải chờ xem. Chủ ngữ là mệnh đề whether (số ít) nên động từ thêm -s: remains.
The idiom “remains to be seen” = we don't know yet. The subject is a whether-clause (singular), so the verb takes -s: remains.

ex2.s: It is unlikely that working life will ever return completely to the way it was before, because many workers now refuse spending two hours a day commuting.
a: It is unlikely that working life will ever return completely to the way it was before, because many workers now refuse to spend two hours a day commuting.
e: refuse + to V (refuse to spend), không đi với V-ing. Ngược lại, spend + thời gian + V-ing (spend two hours commuting) là đúng.
refuse takes to + infinitive (refuse to spend), not -ing. By contrast, spend + time + -ing (spend two hours commuting) is correct.

ex2.s: Đối với nhiều người, lợi ích của việc làm ở nhà rất rõ ràng: không phải đi lại, giờ giấc linh hoạt hơn và có nhiều thời gian hơn cho gia đình.
a: For many people, the benefits of working from home are obvious: no commuting, more flexible hours and more time with their family.
For many people, the benefits of working from home are very clear: no commuting, more flexible hours and more time for their families.
For many people, the advantages of working from home are obvious: no commuting, more flexible working hours and more time with family.
e: “làm ở nhà” → working from home (sau of dùng V-ing). “không phải đi lại” gọn nhất là no commuting, như trong bài đọc. Danh từ benefits số nhiều nên dùng are.
“làm ở nhà” → working from home (-ing after of). “no travelling to work” is best as no commuting, as in the passage. Plural benefits takes are.
f: the benefits of working from home are obvious

q: Viết lại câu bắt đầu bằng “It is unlikely that…”
Rewrite the sentence starting with “It is unlikely that…”
ex2.s: Working life will probably never return completely to the way it was before 2020, even if some managers would like it to.
a: It is unlikely that working life will ever return completely to the way it was before 2020, even if some managers would like it to.
It's unlikely that working life will ever return completely to the way it was before 2020, even if some managers would like it to.
It is unlikely that working life will return completely to the way it was before 2020, even if some managers would like it to.
e: “will probably never” → “It is unlikely that … will ever”. Vì unlikely đã mang nghĩa phủ định, dùng ever thay cho never để tránh phủ định kép.
“will probably never” → “It is unlikely that … will ever”. Unlikely is already negative, so use ever instead of never to avoid a double negative.
f: It is unlikely that working life will ever return

ex2.s: Junior employees|in particular|often say|they miss|the informal learning|that happens|when you sit|next to experienced colleagues.
m: Đặc biệt là nhân viên trẻ thường nói họ nhớ việc học hỏi không chính thức diễn ra khi ngồi cạnh đồng nghiệp giàu kinh nghiệm.
Junior employees in particular often say they miss the informal learning that happens when you sit next to experienced colleagues.
e: “in particular” đứng ngay sau chủ ngữ để nhấn mạnh nhóm này. Mệnh đề quan hệ “that happens…” bổ nghĩa cho “the informal learning”.
“in particular” follows the subject to highlight that group. The relative clause “that happens…” describes “the informal learning”.
